Source, Bargain @COMMENT_BODY@ Buy

•Explore a lively map to find hidden gems. Travel to local neighborhoods or visit the bustling car market to browse inventory. Whether you are looking for a reliable daily driver or a high-end supercar, you need to buy low to sell high.

• Conversational Trading: Utilize a realistic bargaining system to lower buying prices.

• The Trust Factor: Watch out for scammers! Request a detailed vehicle appraisal report or trust your gut before closing the deal.

Repair, Modify @COMMENT_BODY@ Customize

Turn absolute wrecks into highly profitable masterpieces! Bring your inventory to your workshop to boost their market value before listing them for your car selling business.

⚫ Complete Overhauls: Fix body damage, repair engines, wash away filth, and apply fresh paint.

• Custom Tuning: Modify rims, adjust suspensions, add performance upgrades, build custom rides from scratch.

and

Open World Driving @COMMENT_BODY@ Racing

• Take your inventory out of the car showroom and hit the asphalt to test performance firsthand!

• Experience realistic handling with an authentic open world driving engine.

• Push your modified vehicles to their absolute limits on high-speed race tracks to test your tuning setups.

Expand Your Business Empire

• Reinvest your hard-earned profits to scale up your operation. Upgrade your office, decorate your lot, and hire staff to handle more traffic.

• Manage finances using integrated banking, loan, and tax systems.Unlock perks across a massive skill tree to permanently increase your bargaining power, repair speeds, and marketing reach.

Take the wheel, build your destiny, and prove you have what it takes to run the ultimate car dealership.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable car dealership simulator in the existing project based on the user’s feature description.

## Requirements
- Implement car sourcing and bargaining, vehicle appraisal and scam risk, repair and customization, driving and racing, and dealership/finance/skill-tree progression.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game using HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript; game progress is stored in localStorage.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main game interface and styling in `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- Implemented game state, market/dealership views, bargaining and appraisal, workshop actions, listings, upgrades, finance, and a canvas-based driving mode in `game.js`.

### Active
- Finish the JavaScript event handling and app initialization; verify game functionality and browser rendering.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` by wiring navigation and delegated click/change/keyboard/touch event handlers to the implemented game actions and initializing the UI.
2. Run the project and resolve any syntax/runtime issues.
3. Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot; verify responsive usability and core gameplay flow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell and page entry point.
- `styles.css`: Game UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `game.js`: Game logic; currently being built.

## Important Context
- `game.js` currently ends after defining `drawDrive`; event handlers and initial render setup have not yet been added.
- Changes are uncommitted.

- Added responsive styling and game UI components in `styles.css`.

- Run the game, fix syntax/runtime issues, and verify core gameplay and responsive rendering.
- Capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` after `drawDrive` by adding the missing event handling and app initialization.
2. Run the project and resolve any syntax/runtime issues.
3. Verify gameplay and responsive layout, then capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

- `index.html`: App shell and page entry point.
- `styles.css`: Game UI styling and responsive layouts.

- `game.js` now contains substantial view and game-action logic, but event handlers and initial render setup are still missing.

## Objective
- Complete the existing project as a playable car dealership simulator with buying, negotiating, appraising, repairing, driving, and business progression.

## Requirements
- Implement the simulator without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks (viewport at most 1280px wide) and inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Use a self-contained HTML/CSS/vanilla JavaScript browser game with progress saved in localStorage.
- Present it as “Motorhaus,” with dashboard, market, workshop, driving track, and empire views.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the app shell and navigation in `index.html`.
- Added responsive styling and game UI components in `styles.css`.
- Implemented substantial game state, market and dealership rendering, negotiation/appraisal, repairs and tuning, listings, upgrades, loans, skills, day progression, and canvas driving logic in `game.js`.

### Active
- Wire delegated navigation, click/change, keyboard, and touch handlers after `drawDrive` in `game.js`, then initialize the app.
- Run the game, fix syntax/runtime issues, verify core gameplay and responsive rendering, and capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue `game.js` after `drawDrive` with event handling and app initialization.
2. Run the project and resolve any syntax/runtime issues.
3. Verify gameplay and responsive layout, then capture and inspect the latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Main game logic; currently ends after defining `drawDrive`.
- `index.html`: App shell and page entry point.
- `styles.css`: Game UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `capture.sh`: Existing screenshot capture script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- `game.js` has not yet been wired with event handlers or initial render setup; `selectedCarId` is referenced but no declaration was found.
